main_deity: Kṛṣṇa with two consorts Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā
description_en: Mandaḥ Phalcā is raised on a square plinth in Sankhu's quarter Sālkhā Ṭola. Aphalcāwith a square base is generally known as Mandaḥ Phalcā and referred to as amaṇḍapain inscriptions. Usually, such a squarephalcāis open from all four sides and supported by 16 pillars, hence it is known assohrakhuṭṭepāṭī(lit. 16-legged rest house) in Nepali. This particular Mandaḥ Phalcā is the only squarephalcāin Sankhu. Since it features a solid wall facing south it has only ten pillars. The formerly three open sides were closed off with wooden doors to convert the space into a sanctum. It houses stone statues of Kṛṣṇa and his consorts Rukmiṇī and Satyabhāmā. The sanctum also provides space for the Rāma Jhopaḍī Bhajana Maṇḍala, a group of local devotional singers, to sing hymns every day.Historical records from Sankhu refer to this monument as Kumārī Maṇḍapa. This is probably due to the custom of worshipping the Kumārī of Sankhu annually on the ninth day of the dark fortnight of Āśvina. Together with Gaṇeśa and Bhairava, the Kumārī is then given a prominent seat inside the Phalcā. The worship of the three deities in one ritual is also observed in Kathmandu. In Sankhu, however, the Kumarī is also present on the occasion. A Karmācārya priest worships all four of them on behalf of the Kvātha, the arsenal of the medieval period containing a power goddess, of Sankhu.An inscription of 1763 CE (NS 883), installed at the Brahmāyaṇī Pīṭha (SKH0123), states that themaṇḍapaof the Sālkhā Ṭola was renovated and land endowment was made to promote the status of Piunārāyaṇa and his family members of Kathmandu. As this is the onlymaṇḍapathe Sālkhā Ṭola (and the city), it is clear that the renovation refers to this Phalcā. The inscription has probably been moved to the nearby Brahmāyaṇī Pīṭha after its renovation.Currently, the Phalcā is also known as Rāma Jhopaḍī. Senior citizens from the area propose that the statue of Kṛṣṇa, enshrined inside the Phalcā, probably belonged to another temple but was shifted there to prevent it from being unattended. It could well be that the Phalcā came to be known as Rāma Jhopaḍī (lit. Lord Rāma's hut) after the installation of the Vaiṣṇava Statue inside.Abhajanagroup from Golamaḍhī Ṭola in Bhaktapur is connected through its name relation to Rāma Jhopaḍī. They are part of a number ofbhajanagroups in the Kathmandu Valley that subsume under the umbrella term of Hari Bhajana (lit. hymns dedicated to Viṣṇu). Such Vaiṣṇava groups of devotional singers came into existence during the second half of the Rāṇā period. Possibly, this Phalcā in Sankhu also received this name during the same period. The Kṛṣṇa statue in the Phalcā could well be dated back to the late seventeenth or early eighteenth century.The currentbhajanagroup members put photos of various aspects of Kṛṣṇa’s life onKṛṣṇāṣṭamī, the birth anniversary of the deity on display in Mandaḥ Phalcā. They also distribute sweets and pancakes asprasādaof the deity on the celebratory occasion (local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 79). On the day of the Gāījātrā, a cow that is brought from Balaṃpū (Brahmapura) is placed next to the western side of the Phalcā. A brahmin then offers wheat to the cow. After this ritual gesture, the procession in the memory of the deceased can start.In the 2015 earthquakes, the southern base of the Phalcā collapsed. In 2018, the Department of Archaeology dismantled the Phalcā and rebuilt it in neo-traditional style. Following the reconstruction, a smalltulasīmaṭhawas established in front of the Phalcā in memory of the late Vīra Kumāra Śreṣṭha.Two inscriptions  - unrelated to the Phalcā, but significant for the study of Sankhu’s history - are temporarily placed on the plinth of this monument. One of them belongs to the Licchavi period.D. Vajrācārya(VS 2030, p. 508) has published half of this inscription. The other half of the inscription was recovered in 2014, when Gāḥ Hiti (SKH0142), placed behind this Phalca, was renovated. Originally installed in 616 CE (Mānadeva Era 40), the Inscription contains references to a Tṛpura Vihāra and monastic association of the monks of the Mahāsāṅghika (lit. Great Congregation), a Buddhist school of thought (P. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2071, p. 3). Another inscription, originally installed in 1558 CE (NS 679), records the construction of asataḥat Sālkhā Ṭola and the endowment of many plots of land to feed the Jaṅgama ascetics who come from far ("foreign land") at the Sataḥ (N. YogīVS 2012, p. 61-62).
description_ne: साल्खा टोलको केन्द्रस्थलका रूपमा रहेको खुल्ला परिसरमा विविध सम्पदाहरू रहेका छन् जसमध्ये यस फल्चा पनि एक हो । वर्गाकार फल्चा मन्द: फल्चाको स्वरूपमा छ । वर्गाकार जुनसुकै फल्चालाई नेवारीमा ''मन्दः फल्चा'' भन्ने चलन छ भने अभिलेखहरूमा मण्डप लेखिएको पाइन्छ । यस्ता वर्गाकार फल्चामा सोह्रवटा थामो हुने भएकाले थामोको सँख्याका आधारमा यिनलाई नेपालीमा ''सोह्रखुट्टे पाटी'' भन्ने चलन पनि व्याप्त छ । साँखु स्थित यो एकमात्र मण्डपाकारमा निर्मित फल्चा हो । हाल यो वर्गाकार स्वरूपमा भए तापनि सोह्रवटा थामो सहितको खुल्ला मण्डपको स्वरूपमा छैन । चौतर्फी बन्द गरी भित्रको भागलाई गर्भगृहको रूप दिइएको छ र कृष्ण सहित रुक्मिणी र सत्यभामाको शिलामूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । यस कक्षमा साँखुका स्थानीयहरूको सहभागिता रहेको राम झोपडी भजन मण्डल नामक समूहले दैनिक भजन गायन गर्ने गर्दछ ।यस फल्चाको विशेषता भनेको यहाँ प्रति वर्ष असोज कृष्ण नवमीका दिन कुमारी पूजा गरिन्छ । साँखुमा प्राप्त ऐतिहासिक लेखोटहरूमा यस फल्चालाई 'कुमारी मण्डप' भनिएको पाइन्छ । काठमाडौंकै समान कुमारी सहित भैरव र गणेशलाई फल्चाभित्र विराजित गराइन्छ । निवर्तमान कुमारी पनि साथमै विराजित गराइन्छ । साँखुको क्वाथ (कोटघर) बाट पूजा ल्याई कर्माचार्य पूजारीले उपस्थित चारैजनालाई पूज्ने गर्छन् । हाल ब्रह्मायणी पीठमा (SKH0123) भएको  सन् १७६३ (नेसं ८८३) को एक अभिलेखमा कान्तिपुरका पिउनारायण लगायत उनका अन्य परिवार सदस्यहरूको मुक्ति कामनार्थ साल्खा टोलको मण्डप जीर्णोद्धार गरी जग्गा चढाइएको उल्लेख छ । साल्खा टोलमा अवस्थित यो एकमात्र मण्डप भएबाट सो अभिलेखले यही मण्डपको जीर्णोद्धारलाई जनाएको देखिन्छ । कुनै कारणवस मण्डपको अभिलेख कालान्तरमा यही टोलको ब्रम्हायणी पीठमा स्थानान्तरण भएको देखिन्छ । विगतका लिखित सामग्रीमा मण्डप भनिएको यस फल्चा हाल साँखुमा ''राम झोपडी'' नामले प्रख्यात छ । फल्चाभित्र कतैबाट ल्याई राखिएको कृष्ण मूर्ति छ । यसरी वैष्णव मूर्ति स्थापना गरी यहाँ भजनको प्रचलन चले पश्चात मात्र ''राम झोपडी'' नाम अस्तित्वमा आएको हुन सक्दछ । भक्तपुरको गोलमढी टोलमा पनि समान ''राम झोपडी'' नाम गरेको भजन मण्डली छ । उपत्यकामा 'हरि भजन' नामले चिनिने मण्डलीहरू पनि रहेका छन् । यस्ता वैष्णव नाम दिइएका मण्डलीहरू राणाकालको उत्तरार्धतिर मात्र अस्तित्वमा आएका देखिन्छन् जुन नामहरू नेवारी वा नेपाली भाषाका अनुकुल छैनन् । साँखु स्थित यस फल्चाले पनि नयाँ नाम  यसै ताका पाएको प्रतीत हुन्छ । सन् २०१५ को भूकम्पले फल्चाको जगका रूपमा रहेको पछाडिको गारो भत्किएको थियो । जगमै क्षति पुगेकाले यसलाई पूर्णत: भत्काई पुरात्तव विभागले सन् २०१८ (विसं २०७४)  मा परम्परागत शैलीमै पुन:निर्माण गरेको हो । पुन:निर्माण पश्चात् फल्चाको अग्र भागमा दिवंगत वीर कुमार श्रेष्ठको नाममा तुलसीको सानो आकरको मठ थपिएको हो ।फल्चाभित्र रहेको कृष्ण मूर्ति १७ औं शदीको अन्त्य वा १८ औं शदीतिरको देखिन्छ । साँखुकै कुनै मन्दिरभित्रको मूर्ति कालान्तरमा अलपत्र परेकाले यहाँ ल्याई स्थापना गरेको अनुमान स्थानीय बृद्धहरू लगाउँछन् । भजन मण्डलले कृष्णाष्टमीका दिन फल्चामा कृष्णको जीवनीसंग सम्बन्धित तस्विरहरू प्रदर्शनीमा राख्ने र स्वारी, माल्पा-पुरी जस्ता रोटीहरू प्रसादका रूपमा वितरण गर्ने थिति रहेको छ (local knowledge, local resident, Śreṣṭha, male, age 79) । गाइजात्राको दिन साँखुको बलंपुलिबाट (ब्रह्मपुर) गाई ल्याई यस फल्चाको पश्चिमी पेटीमुनि राखिन्छ । सोही स्थानमा राखी गाईलाई ब्राह्मणबाट गहुँ खुवाउनुपर्ने चलन रहेको छ । यस कार्यको समापन पछिमात्र गाईजात्राको झाँकी निस्कन मिल्ने मान्यता साँखुमा पाइन्छ ।यस फल्चासंग असम्बन्धित तर साँखुको इतिहासमा ठुलो महत्व राख्ने दुई अभिलेख अस्थयी रूपमा फल्चाको पेटीमा राखिएका छन् । दुईमध्ये एक लिच्छविकालको हो । धनवज्रले साँखुको अभिलेख' शीर्षकमा यस अभिलेखको आधा अंशमात्र प्रकाशमा ल्याएका छन् (D. VajrācāryaVS 2030, p. 508)। सन् २०१४ (विसं २०७१) सालमा यस फल्चा पछाडीको हिति जीर्णोद्धार गर्ने क्रममा बाँकी आधा अंश फेला परेको हो। सन् ६१६ (मानदेव संवत् ४०) को यस अभिलेखमा तृपुर विहार र महा सांघिक भिक्षुसंघको कुरा परेकोले साँखुमा बौद्ध धर्मको ऐतिहासिकताको दृष्टिले यो अभिलेखले ठुलो महत्व राख्दछ (P. ŚreṣṭhaVS 2071, p. 3) । त्यसैगरी अर्को अभिलेख सन् १५५८ (नेसं ६७९) को हो जसमा साल्खा टोलमा सत: बनाई 'जतीजंगम योगी परदेशी' हरूलाई विभिन्न अवसरमा सत:मा राखी भोजन गराउन प्रशस्त जग्गा दान भएको कुरा उल्लेख छ (N. YogīVS 2012, p. 61-62)।

historical_events.event_description: The inscription, though not connected to the Phalcā, has been temporarily placed in front of its northern plinth. The Licchavi inscription dated 616 CE (Mānadeva Era 40) is significant for the study of Sankhu’s history.D. Vajrācārya(VS 2030, p. 508) has published the left side of the broken inscription. The second half of the Inscription was only recovered in 2014 CE, when Gāḥ Hiti (SKH0142), located behind this Phalca, was renovated. The Inscription contains references to a Tṛpura Vihāra and monastic association of the monks of the Mahāsāṅghika (lit. Great Congregation), a Buddhist school of thought.

historical_events.event_name: Construction of a sataḥ and endowment of land.
historical_events.event_description: The inscription dated 1558 CE (NS 679) records the construction of asataḥat the Sālkhā Ṭola and endowment of many plots of land, providing income to feed the Jaṅgama ascetics who are said to have come from abroad.This inscription from the Malla period kept next to the eastern plinth is not related to Mandaḥ Phalcā.

An inscription of 1763 CE (NS 883) installed at the Brahmāyaṇī Pīṭha (SKH0123) states that the ‘maṇḍapa’ of the Sālkhā Ṭola was renovated and a land endowment was made to manifest and improve the status of Piunārāyaṇa and his family from Kathmandu. As this is the onlymaṇḍapain Sālkhā Ṭola, it is clear that the renovation refers to it. The Inscription was probably shifted to the nearby Brahmāyaṇī Pīṭha later.
The southern plinth and wall of the monument were badly damaged during the 2015 earthquakes.
The Phalca was demolished and rebuilt by the Department of Archaeology after the 2015 earthquakes.
On the occasion of completion of the restoration, atulasī maṭhawas added in the name of late Vīra Kumāra Śreṣṭha.
